title: Platform-wide slowness and 429s
executive_summary: INC-011 (SEV2) was a platform-wide latency and HTTP 429 event affecting api-gateway, auth-service and user-service, with symptoms starting at 20:00Z. The investigation status is PROBABLE_ROOT_CAUSE with confidence 0.58, meaning this is the most probable explanation rather than a confirmed fact. The leading hypothesis (H1) is a client-side retry storm from mobile-ios-7.4.0: the gateway rate limiter logged a WARN at 19:55:11Z stating that 363% of requests from this client were retries with Retry-After ignored (logpat-api-gateway-d39f8491). Gateway, auth-service and user-service request rates all stepped up at 19:55:00Z (+138%, +133%, +134% respectively; met-api-gateway-request_rate-1930-2030, met-auth-service-request_rate-1930-2030, met-user-service-request_rate-1930-2030). Gateway p95 latency and error rate rose at 19:56:00Z, and the first 429 was returned at 19:56:06Z (logpat-api-gateway-8a499a8e). Clients kept retrying, sustaining load through about 20:25Z. The user-service 7.1.3 release (19:48Z) and an edge/load-balancer change were rejected based on timing and metrics. The initial trigger of the mobile retries before 19:55Z was not identified.

hypotheses.description: A client-side retry storm from mobile-ios-7.4.0 began before 19:55Z. The gateway rate limiter throttled it, producing the 429s. The traffic step then loaded auth-service and user-service, which caused the latency rises. Mechanism: Trigger outside the observed services -> mobile-ios-7.4.0 retries at ~363-396% of normal volume with Retry-After ignored (first limiter WARN 19:55:11Z) -> gateway, auth and user request rates step up ~+105-138% at 19:55 -> gateway CPU rises and p95 latency rises at 19:56 -> gateway rate limiter returns 429s (first logged 19:56:06Z) -> clients keep retrying, sustaining load through 20:25.

critic_review.summary: Leading hypothesis H1 (mobile-ios-7.4.0 retry storm loading the gateway, then auth and user-service, with 429s from the gateway rate limiter) is the best-supported explanation. The client-attributed limiter WARN (19:55:11Z) precedes the first 429 (19:56:06Z), and the gateway, auth and user request-rate steps all start at 19:55:00Z, one minute before the latency and error onsets at 19:56. payment-service and redis are flat, so the surge is not platform-wide. My own checks found no api-gateway config change and no api-gateway deployment in 19:00-20:30Z, which weakens H3. The only user-service deploy (19:48Z, H2) is contradicted: user-service p95 was flat from 19:30 to 19:55 and auth-service shows the same step without any dependency on user-service. H4 is contradicted by the log attribution of the surge to one client. The pre-19:55 log scan found no mobile-ios-7.4.0 errors or other trigger, so what initially prompted retries is unexplained. The 1700-9500 rps figure conflicts with the 77 req/min routed count and needs reconciling, but it does not undermine the time ordering.

assessments.reasoning: Client-attributed retry WARN at 19:55:11Z precedes the 429s at 19:56:06Z. Gateway, auth and user request-rate steps align at 19:55 and latency/error onsets follow at 19:56. Payment and redis are flat. The initial retry trigger and the rps discrepancy are open limitations, not contradictions.

user-service p95 was flat (75-83 ms) from 19:30-19:55 after the 19:48 deploy, and the rise starts at 19:56 after the traffic step. There is no error change, and auth-service shows the same step without depending on user-service. The pre-check flagged this as correlation only.

No api-gateway config change or deployment appears in the config and deployment records for 19:00-20:30Z. The limiter WARN and the traffic step both precede the first 429, so load, not a new threshold, is the better-timed cause. The config store is not authoritative for the gateway, but the timing evidence already disfavours this.

The gateway logs attribute the excess to a single client (mobile-ios-7.4.0, retries with Retry-After ignored), which points to client behaviour rather than an edge or LB routing change. No edge or LB evidence supports a routing change.

conclusion: The most probable explanation for INC-011 is a retry storm from mobile-ios-7.4.0 that began before 19:55Z. The gateway rate limiter throttled it, producing 429s from 19:56Z, while the traffic step loaded auth-service and user-service and drove latency increases. This conclusion is supported by timing, per-client log attribution and flat payment-service and redis traffic, but it is not confirmed. Open gaps include the unexplained trigger for the initial retries, the unreconciled rps figures, and an inferred rather than traced dependency path. The user-service 7.1.3 release and an edge/LB change were rejected, and an unrecorded gateway config change remains a lower-likelihood alternative.
